text:
Oh, wait! No, no, no! 

There *was*, in fact, a black woman who hurt me in life. I had completely forgotten about her!

Over a year ago, I journaled about a high school teacher who was grooming me, borderline pedophilic. She was my homeroom teacher, and positioned herself as a mentor figure while I was trying to understand girls in high school.

("Homeroom" was not a real class; it's just for 15-minute roll calls for tracking attendance before you go to your actual classes that day.)

She remained a "friend" per se, clear up until I returned home from the military. She would always leave comments on (what was then...) my MySpace page about how attractive I was and that I should keep my head up. When I went temporarily homeless, she offered me a place to stay...a small room, but one that I was grateful for. 

I had no complaints and thought she was a saint. The plan was to pay her rent from my GI Bill benefits while I finished college and got back on my feet.

To thank her, I invited her to a Hibachi restaurant with whatever other friends would celebrate my homecoming. And during the dinner, she sat next to me and whispered in my ear that I have an open mind but that I should open my heart as well.

I had *zero* idea what she was referring to. But I smiled, nodded, and said that I'd consider her advice...just to be nice.

She even *told* me, flat-out, without me asking, that I could bring a girl over.

I thought "Cool! You always were one of the cool teachers!"

...so? I did. 🤷‍♂️

One night, I brought home a date. Blonde. She didn't mind that I was technically homeless.

We spent the night by the fireplace. And, in the morning, I drove her home. Simple. 

We weren't loud. We were very respectful. I honored the rules. 

I wasn't trying to burn any bridges.

I walk back in through the front door after returning the girl home to find my things packed and sitting by the door with a long text message that made no coherent sense, either grammatically or substantively.

...it legitimately seemed like gibberish, and she made references to things I had no idea about. I had no idea what she was talking about. It seemed like a schizophrenic tirade.

What did I do? 

I didn't argue. I didn't say a word of complaint.

I took my things right from the position on the floor they had been packed and sat in and left.

Easy.

No yelling. Not even a disagreement. 

I walked in after taking the blonde home. Saw my things. Saw the text message. Said nothing. And walked back out the door within ten minutes. 

A little while later, the teacher sent me a very apologetic message saying that she knew I had done nothing wrong or against what we agreed. 

I cordially told her I understood, but that I would not be returning. 

And that was it. 

*Years* later, like a moron, I *finally* realized what the deal was: That teacher had been trying to seduce me since *teenhood*. She was technically grooming me and, if I had reciprocated, no doubt she would have had relations with me during high school.

When I was an adult, she saw my homelessness as an opportunity, and saying I could bring a girl over wasn't a real invite but a test. And by "open[ing] my heart" at the hibachi dinner, she was talking about *her*, lol! 🤣

I had just *friendzoned* her without thinking anything of it.

You have to understand: She was well over 20 years older than me (possibly 30), with already graying hair. And, not that I wasn't open to providing pleasure to an older woman as a horny military guy (hey, just being honest... high-testosterone Marines, Navy, etc. know...).

So, it wasn't her age; she just legitimately wasn't my type.

And I didn't truly view myself as attractive enough to be hit on in that way. I didn't even consider it as a possibility. 

I thought she was just being friendly and supportive of my emotional health the way a good teacher would be. 

But...apparently...that wasn't the case. 🤷‍♂️

And I do think race was the key component there, because I was certainly attracted to other teachers. And I remember one time that I was on MySpace (years ago) talking about how I'd knock the dust off of Madonna's old ass... (which was about twenty years ago, so the Madonna then was still far better than what she turned into. It was the "Frozen" era Madonna.)

...and that teacher snapped on me in a way that didn't make sense at the time. 

She made me feel like I was a horrible person and I didn't know why. I apologized to her and I didn't even understand what it was that I was apologizing for; I just didn't want her to be angry with me.

And I think that's what it was: I completely blocked her out of my mind as a romantic or sexual option. Zero attraction. Nothing.

...and I think at the end she came to realize that hurting me for not being attracted to her is *still* not going to make me attracted to her. 

And she realized she had started becoming cruel. Putting me out on the street over a date I had with a woman she *told me ahead of time* that I could have. (That I wouldn't have even had, because my default assumption was to *not* bring girls over...)

Pro-blacks immediately assume that my attraction to European women is because black women were mean to me.

...not in the slightest. 

Black women were but background noise to me as I grew up. They weren't who I came home to after school; they weren't the village that raised me. 

And while, yes, one hurt me...

...it was because I already wasn't attracted to her. Not the other way around.

And even her, I had almost entirely forgotten.

Beneath the Noise of a National Emergency

I wasn’t planning to write about a national emergency this.But after watching what’s unfolded over the last few days, I couldn’t quite turn my attention back to what I’d originally intended.

Friday the 13th brought a nationwide grounding of departing aircraft. Microsoft systems serving government offices, Congress, and the courts had been experiencing widespread disruptions. A tanker struck a docked passenger vessel in New Orleans, leaving it on its side in the Mississippi River. In Peoria, Illinois, an explosive device was discovered at an industrial facility, forcing evacuations while authorities searched for anything else that might pose a threat.

There were other troubling developments during the week, including reports of senior administration officials relocating to military housing because of security concerns.

Individually, these events have their own explanations. Some may have absolutely nothing to do with one another.

But as I watched them accumulate, I found myself moving into pattern recognition mode. I began looking at the timing, the systems being affected, and whether there might be connections that weren’t immediately apparent.

Then Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin spoke during the aviation shutdown briefing.

He referred to continuity of government, confirmed the activation of FEMA resources, and described the situation as a national emergency.

That got my attention.

The explanation being offered was a telecommunications failure. According to Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, aging equipment had become overloaded, affecting radar and communications systems across the country.

But questions were already circulating about what actually caused the shutdown, including concerns attributed to air traffic controllers.

And I couldn’t help wondering whether something else might have been taking place.

Could restricting departures have served another purpose? Could it have been useful during a security operation involving people who might otherwise leave the country?

I have no proof of that. It’s a possibility I’ve considered.

And given what we know about government operations that remained hidden for years, I don’t think it’s unreasonable to examine possibilities beyond the first explanation we’re given.

What struck me about this particular week was how many different systems seemed to be affected.

Air travel stopped. Digital services failed. Thousands of people suddenly found themselves dependent on decisions being made somewhere beyond their reach.

We’ve built an extraordinary civilization around systems we rarely think about until they stop working.

Electricity, communications, transportation, banking. Nearly everything we do now depends on infrastructure most of us have never seen and couldn’t operate independently.

We call it the grid, although the electrical grid is only one part of a much larger network of dependencies.

And we’ve become remarkably comfortable with that arrangement.

I topped off my gas tank Saturday morning.

I wasn’t expecting anything specific to happen. I simply considered the possibility of a power interruption and what that would mean if the pumps stopped working.

A small decision. Nothing dramatic.

But I noticed why I was making it.

A few days earlier, I probably wouldn’t have given it a second thought.

That’s what interests me about these periods of uncertainty. Something can shift in the way we’re observing the world even when nothing in our immediate surroundings appears to have changed.

The lights are still on. The grocery stores are open. People are going about their lives.

Yet we’re watching things more closely. Listening differently to official announcements. Looking for patterns in events we might ordinarily have dismissed as unrelated.

And after years of one emergency following another, I wonder how much of our consciousness has become accustomed to remaining on alert.

How much of our attention is now occupied with anticipating the next disruption?

Pattern recognition is part of how we navigate the world. It helps us notice changes and sometimes recognize connections before we fully understand them.

Intuition belongs in that conversation too. I’ve relied on mine throughout my life, and I’m not inclined to dismiss what I’m sensing simply because I can’t immediately explain it.

But I also recognize that expectation can influence what we notice.

When we’re already anticipating something, each new event can begin to look like another piece of the same puzzle.

That makes discernment especially important. We need to be able to recognize a possible pattern without deciding too quickly what it means.

And I think that becomes harder when we’re rarely given any real pause between emergencies.

There’s another aspect of this week that deserves attention.

The machinery of government continues operating whether we can see what it’s doing or not.

Emergency plans, intelligence operations, security protocols, and preparations exist for circumstances most Americans hope never to experience.

Continuity of government is part of that framework. It was designed to ensure essential government functions could survive extraordinary events.

Mullin’s remarks don’t establish that a formal continuity operation was activated. His description of a national emergency also doesn’t constitute a new presidential declaration.

But I paid attention to his choice of words, and to the scale of the federal response he described.

Emergency authority can change how decisions are made, how resources are deployed, and what government agencies are permitted to do.

We’ve seen existing emergency declarations used to expand military responsibilities, including the April 2025 directive involving federal lands along the southern border.

That action was separate from this week’s events. Still, it demonstrates how emergency powers can extend into areas most citizens rarely examine.

And then there’s Operation CHAOS.

The original CIA program was real. It gathered intelligence on Americans involved in antiwar movements and accumulated extensive domestic surveillance records. It was officially terminated in 1974.

Its termination doesn’t mean similar activity could never occur again, under that name or another.

Whether anything resembling it is taking place now remains an open question. Nothing we’ve seen establishes a connection to this week’s disruptions.

But history has shown us that some government activities become fully visible only years after they occurred.

That history is part of why I continue asking questions.

I’ve been thinking about what it means to recognize a turning point while you’re still living through it.

History is easier to understand afterward. We look back and identify the warnings, the unusual circumstances, the decisions that changed everything.

But the people living through those moments didn’t know how the story would unfold.

They were going to work, buying groceries, paying bills, and trying to make sense of the news.

Some recognized that something was changing. Others saw nothing particularly unusual. And some undoubtedly connected events that later turned out to be unrelated.

We don’t have the advantage of hindsight while we’re living through our own time.

Maybe that’s why I find the condition of continuous alertness so troubling.

Our attention begins moving ahead of our lives. We’re physically here, doing ordinary things, while part of our consciousness is occupied with what might be happening elsewhere or what could happen next.

I wonder how much that changes our ability to perceive clearly.

If we’re constantly looking for the next emergency, do we eventually lose the ability to recognize when we’re no longer in one?

And when something genuinely unusual does happen, how do we distinguish it from all the other warnings competing for our attention?

I don’t have an answer to that.

I don’t know whether the events of this week are connected. I don’t know whether additional information will reveal something larger taking place behind them.

But I’m not prepared to dismiss the questions simply because the immediate disruption has passed.

The planes are flying again. Microsoft’s services have been restored. The evacuation in Peoria has been lifted.

Ordinary life resumes.

And that’s the part I keep thinking about.

How quickly we return to normal, even when we haven’t fully understood what interrupted it.

A few days from now, these events may already be disappearing beneath another set of headlines.

I wonder how many questions will disappear with them.

text:
Cato: 
A dramatic, cheeky three-paragraph recounting of Addison’s Cato, delivered in the lofty, powdered-wig cadence of the Revolutionary age by Hamilton, Washington, and Jefferson:
Alexander Hamilton: Gentlemen, mark ye well the tale of noble Cato—that stubborn Roman who would sooner freeze his bones in Utica than bend the knee to Caesar’s gilded tyranny! Picture the fellow, all stern virtue and unyielding principle, rallying his senators like a Continental Congress that hath refused every last cup of tea, while the tyrant’s legions draw nigh with the subtlety of a redcoat tax collector. He speaks of liberty as if it were a sacred compact written in the stars themselves, and his friends (those soft-hearted fools) plead with him to flee or strike a bargain; yet Cato, with a wit sharper than any bayonet, declares he’d rather die free than live a slave to one man’s ambition—though between us, he might have saved himself a world of trouble had he simply accepted a pension and a quiet farm in the provinces.
George Washington: Aye, and mark how the drama unfolds with all the solemn thunder of a winter camp at Valley Forge! Caesar’s emissaries arrive bearing offers of mercy that smell suspiciously of chains, while Cato’s own son—hot-blooded youth that he is—nearly ruins the enterprise by loving the wrong maiden and picking quarrels fit for a tavern brawl. The great man holds firm, however, choosing death by his own hand rather than surrender, a gesture so grand and so thoroughly Roman that even the most skeptical among us must admit it stirs the blood; one almost fancies the author wrote it expressly so that we might quote it while marching, though I confess the final act is rather heavy on the monologues and light on the practical business of winning a war.
Thomas Jefferson: And thus the curtain falls upon Cato’s fall, a tragedy that flatters every rebel heart with its portrait of virtue triumphant even in defeat—yet one cannot help smiling at the sheer theatrical excess of it all. Here is a man who lectures the heavens on republican purity while his household frets over unpaid debts and romantic intrigues, a spectacle so perfectly suited to our age that we Founders have adopted its lines as readily as we adopted the Declaration’s. Still, let us not be too solemn: Caesar wins the field, Cato wins the epilogue, and the audience goes home convinced that dying for liberty is infinitely more fashionable than living under a crown—provided, of course, that someone else is left to write the history and settle the accounts.

text:
I am unconvinced there's a vast problem. There's a ton of anecdotes, but no data offered to support the assertion of VAST fraud/overclaiming/etc.

I am unconvinced that millions of veterans need to be put through a screening program as a matter of first priority. Deal with the huge civilian kleptocracy first. Then take a peek at the vets. Maybe.

Grok say:

Over-claiming for minor or mild conditions is common and structurally encouraged; outright fraud involving non-existent conditions is real but limited in proven scale.

Distinction Between the Two

Non-existent / intentional fraud: Claiming a condition that does not exist, or fabricating severe impairment (e.g., paralysis, legal blindness, or total unemployability when surveillance shows otherwise). These cases are prosecuted when clear evidence (video, contradictory medical records, etc.) is available.
Over-claiming for minor or low-impairment conditions: Real diagnoses (or plausible ones) that are service-connected under VA rules, but are mild, treatable, common in the general population, or have limited effect on employability. The rating schedule still assigns compensation, and multiple such conditions can be stacked.
Extent of Non-Existent / Outright Fraud

Proven cases remain few relative to program size. VA OIG opens on the order of ~60 investigations per year specifically into suspected compensation fraud by veterans. Convictions across relevant categories are typically under 200 per year against millions of claims processed and ~6.3–6.9 million recipients. OIG leadership has stated there is no “massive fraud,” and veterans suspected of compensation fraud represent only a small share (~3.7%) of active investigations (most OIG work targets other schemes).⁠Military⁠Stripes

A 2025 Washington Post review of dozens of prosecutions since 2017 found clear cases of faking severe disabilities, but these represent a tiny fraction of the overall program. Detection is low because OIG prioritizes cases with strong evidence; subjective or hard-to-disprove claims are rarely pursued. The true rate of intentional fraud is almost certainly higher than the prosecution rate, but available evidence does not support it as widespread or a dominant cost driver.

Extent of Over-Claiming for Minor Conditions

This is far more prevalent. The Washington Post investigation reported large numbers of service-connected ratings for conditions that rarely prevent work or daily function:

~556,000 for eczema/dermatitis
~332,000 for hemorrhoids
~110,000 for benign skin growths
~81,000 for acne
~74,000 for varicose veins
Tinnitus is the single most prevalent service-connected disability (millions of veterans; consistently the top condition in VBA reports) and is rated at a flat 10% regardless of severity.⁠Atlantadisability⁠Washington Post

These numbers come from VA data. Many such conditions are legitimately linked to service (noise exposure for tinnitus; physical demands, diet, or stress for hemorrhoids or skin issues), and the rating schedule explicitly provides for them (e.g., hemorrhoids up to 20%, skin conditions often 0–30% for milder cases). However:

Average number of service-connected disabilities per recipient has risen to ~7.3 (from ~4.7 a decade earlier).
Combined ratings have shifted sharply upward: in FY2025, ~29% of recipients were at 100%, with another large share at 70–90%. The nonlinear combined ratings table means several low-percentage conditions can meaningfully raise the overall payment.⁠Vetrify⁠Vsgsolutions
Private for-profit consultants and online communities actively coach veterans to claim hard-to-disprove or high-value conditions (migraines, certain mental health issues, erectile dysfunction, sleep apnea, etc.) and to maximize stacking. OIG has flagged elevated fraud-risk indicators on public (private-provider) Disability Benefits Questionnaires.
The system is deliberately pro-claimant: the benefit-of-the-doubt rule, limited reexaminations for many conditions, and acceptance of veteran statements for subjective symptoms favor granting claims. Processing accuracy issues exist (OIG has found error rates of 30%+ in some targeted samples for issues like scar ratings or reductions), but most errors are administrative rather than evidence of widespread veteran fabrication.

Overall Assessment of Extent

Non-existent fraud: Low proven extent (well under 1% of recipients or claims based on investigations and convictions). True incidence is higher but remains a minority phenomenon; it is not the primary driver of program growth or cost.
Over-claiming of minor/mild conditions: Substantial and systemic. Millions of ratings fall into categories that public perception would view as minor. When stacked, they contribute to the large share of recipients at high combined ratings and to the rapid growth in the program (alongside legitimate factors such as the PACT Act’s expanded presumptives for toxic exposures, greater awareness, and aging of the veteran population).
Individual low-rated conditions pay relatively modest amounts (often $150–500 per month), so their standalone fiscal impact is limited. The larger effect comes from volume plus combination into higher overall ratings. This reflects both the statutory design of the program (compensation for any ratable service-connected impairment, not solely for unemployability) and practical incentives that encourage claiming everything possible.

In short, pure fraud involving fabricated non-existent disabilities is uncommon by available measures, while over-claiming and maximizing compensation for real but minor or low-impairment conditions is widespread and built into how the system operates.

text:
Backpack Wins CFTC Approval, Four Years After FTX's Fall

The exchange that bought FTX's European arm can now offer leveraged crypto perpetual futures to US traders.

Four years after FTX collapsed, a company that picked up part of its remains has won a key green light from Washington. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has officially approved Backpack, allowing it to offer leveraged crypto perpetual futures in the United States, with trades settled on the blockchain.

CFTC Chair Michael Selig called the decision "an important milestone in the evolution of American financial markets."

The company's story has some familiar threads. CEO Armani Ferrante previously worked at Alameda Research, while the US arm is led by Mark Wetjen, a former acting CFTC chair.

Backpack is not alone. Last week, tZERO secured a similar approval from the CFTC.

text:
Tiny radioactive seeds implanted straight into the brain cleared away visible glioblastoma tumors in five patients — and every patient treated in the trial is still alive.

The treatment, called Alpha DaRT, places seeds loaded with radium-224 directly inside the tumor during surgery. 

As the radium decays it throws off alpha particles, a short-range, extremely destructive radiation that shreds the DNA of cells within a few millimeters and then fades, hitting the tumor hard without irradiating the rest of the brain. In the REGAIN trial at the Ohio State University Comprehensive Cancer Center, eight people with recurrent glioblastoma have been treated and six have had response scans. 

All six responded: five had a complete response, meaning no measurable tumor left on imaging, and the sixth's tumor shrank by 58%. As of November 11, all eight were still alive.

Glioblastoma is the brain cancer that kills most of the people it touches. Median survival is around eight months, only about 7% of patients are alive five years later, and when the tumor returns after surgery and radiation there is very little left to offer. A single procedure that wipes a recurrent tumor off the scans would be a real shift in what doctors can do.

That said, this is the company's own interim announcement covering eight patients, presented as a conference poster rather than a peer-reviewed paper, and three of the six responses still need confirming on later scans. Also, four of the six developed radiation necrosis, dead and inflamed tissue at the treatment site, and in two cases scans cannot yet tell necrosis from the tumor growing back. Alpha Tau is enrolling toward 20 patients, which it says may be enough to support a submission to regulators.

source: Alpha Tau Medical. (2026). New positive interim results from its U.S. Alpha DaRT recurrent glioblastoma trial [Press release]. REGAIN interim data presented at the 31st Annual Meeting of the Society for Neuro-Oncology.

Semiconductor research firm SemiAnalysis has sharply LOWERED its global AI accelerator capital expenditure forecasts, with cuts of up to 41%:

2027: $770B → $627B (-19%)
2028: $1.054T → $758B (-28%)
2029: $1.352T → $796B (-41%)
2030: $1.531T → $923B (-40%)

That's a $608 billion reduction in its 2030 forecast alone.

SemiAnalysis also cut its cumulative 2026-2030 accelerator silicon shipment area forecast by 17%, with Nvidia accounting for 66% of that reduction.

Its 2028 HBM shipment forecast was lowered from 9.0 to 6.4 exabytes, a 30% reduction, while projected 2030 AI accelerator power demand fell from 122.8 GW to 80.7 GW, down 34%.

The firm cited slowing revenue growth at frontier AI labs, tighter capital markets, and lower assumptions for future chip and memory pricing.

Importantly, even after these cuts, SemiAnalysis still expects annual AI accelerator spending to more than double from $392 billion in 2026 to $923 billion by 2030.

text:
### MY BROTHER SOLD OUR LATE FATHER'S CAR AND KEPT THE MONEY

When our father died, he left behind an old car that all four of us siblings agreed should be sold and the money shared equally.

The car was valued at $12,000.

My older brother, Andrew, volunteered to handle the sale because he claimed he knew someone who would pay a good price.

Two weeks later, he called us and announced that he had sold it for $9,000.

He said the buyer had negotiated aggressively and that we should accept the offer.

We agreed to divide the money into four equal shares of $2,250.

I received my payment, as did my two sisters.

Something didn't sit right with me, though. I later contacted the buyer to ask about the car because I was considering purchasing a similar model.

BRANIFF HISTORY TODAY - On this day, November 16, 1959, Braniff International Airways inaugurated the first Jet-Powered Lockheed L-188 Electra Jet service between Texas and Colorado Springs and Denver. Braniff, on June 15, had commenced the carrier's first Electra Flights from San Antonio to Dallas, and New York and from Houston to Dallas and Chicago.

Braniff's new service linked the Rocky Mountain region and the Southwest with fast and efficient jet-powered service. The new Electra Flights operated over a route from San Antonio to Dallas Love Field to Amarillo, Texas, with continuing service to Colorado Springs and Denver, Colorado. The 450 mile-per-hour cruising speed of the Electra four-engine turboprop gave passengers flying between Dallas and Amarillo the fastest air service ever offered between the two Texas cities.

Impressive flight times were a hallmark of the new Electra Flights. Only 67 minutes flight time was required over the 333 mile distance between Amarillo and Dallas. Flight time between Amarillo and Denver was a quick 74 minutes over the 359 mile distance. Braniff offered one daily roundtrip over the route with a morning northbound departure and a mid-afternoon return flight.

A large group of local civic and military officials were on board the inaugural flight. Guest included service personnel from the Colorado Springs Air Force Academy and city officials including the City Manager. Representatives from Lockheed also accompanied the flight to ensure that it went without problem. Braniff Electra Ship N9703C flew the inaugural flight from Dallas to Denver.

Photo: Braniff International Lockheed L-188 Electra registered as N9709C is taxiing at Kansas City Municipal Airport in 1967. The aircraft is painted in the 1967 Alexander Girard/Harper and George Panagra Red Solid Color Scheme with White Wings, Engines and Tail with Alexander Girard Sky Font and BI Tail Logo in Black. This aircraft flew the inaugural flight that introduced Electra Jet service between Dallas and Denver with intermediate stop at Amarillo and Colorado Springs on November 16, 1959.

text:
Couldn't go home this year.
Firmly establishing myself as the black sheep of the family 😢

But let me explain why Chhath Pooja is a big deal.
And why it is my favourite festival. 
Here is why 

👇

1. 
Chhath is a festival of faith unlike any other.

There are no stringent rules.
There is no mahurat.
There is no pandit ji.
You don't have to go to a temple.
No specific mantras or pooja or havan. 

This is a festival of individual faith.
 A prayer that brings together the softest of things - the heart of a mother..
with the mightiest of elements - the Sun..

There is no conduit - no Panditji, no specific place of worship, no chanting of hard-to-know mantras, no stringent rules and process gatekept by anyone

Women (my dadi, my mom, my aunts) stand in any water body, in the cold,  before the sun rises, praying to the sun. 
They murmur silent prayers for everyone's well being.
There is no loud music or lud chants
Just a woman with irrational faith and a soft prayer for their kids and families and community.

2. 
 You can do chhath even if you have nothing to offer to the deity (Sun).
There is no defined offering, no sweets, dry fruits, no dakshina to offer to panditiji.

You just offer water to the sun if you have nothing else.
In hindi we call it ' Suraj ko argh dena'

If you have the means you offer whatever fruits are locally available.

There is scant difference in how the richest perform this festival, versus the poorest.

It is truly, a festival for EVERYONE 
The only thing you need is faith and good vibes

3. 
Chhath is unique in that it celebrates and worships both the rising sun and the setting sun.
The same prayers are offered to both

The whole world pays homage to the rising sun- symbolic of the powerful, mighty, on their way up.

Chhath reminds us to value the  setting sun too ❤️

Paying homage who came before us, and past their prime, and whose shoulders we stand.

It is also a symbolic gesture to remind us of impermanence.
What rises up, sets down and rises again. 
And both who are rising and setting deserve our homage and prayers and kindness

4. 
It is truly a community festival.
Many people you see in this photo are not family, but from the local community.
For 4 days people flock to the homes where chhath Pooja happens.
People come to help.
 Pooja is hard on the ones doing it ~ 4 days of fasting, last 2 days fasting without water.
If someone is not able to fast and pray, they try to participate by association.
By helping, and by doing the pooja -via the ones who are fasting and praying

My house in Ranchi is buzzing with people for 4 days - with folks from the community, friends-from near and far.
People come to seek blessings from the ones praying, to help, chit-chat and most importantly, to get prasaad

The faith is strong  :)

And there is an unsaid rule in our part of the world -
" You can be a moron, good-for-nothing son all year

But if you come home for chhath, and help decorate the ghaat (water body) and do the service and  participate in the faith, all is forgotten and forgiven.

And you qualify for the best blessings from the kindest warmest, hearts brimming with faith.. like only a mom's heart can be  ❤️❤️"

Jai Chhathi Maiyya 
Happy Chhath pooja to all

When a non-local signal, a seed memory, or a residual environmental field needs to be clothed quickly so the nervous system can register it without shock, the brain frequently selects these ancient channels. They already know how to evoke instant recognition without requiring a long, exhausting explanation. A single phantom scent can deliver an entire atmosphere in one inhalation. The Moral Laundering of Shraadh: When Ritual Masks Neglect
There is a particular kind of theatre that plays out with predictable regularity in affluent drawing rooms and temple courtyards across India. Heirs who spent years too busy to visit an aging parent, too distracted to sit by a sickbed, and too indifferent to offer basic companionship suddenly discover a profound sense of filial duty the moment the funeral pyre cools. Out come the elaborate arrangements for Shraadh—the meticulously curated feasts for priests, the solemn invitations, the public performance of grief and piety.
Let us call this what it is: not an act of spiritual devotion, but an exercise in public relations and moral laundering. It is an attempt to purchase post-mortem absolution for real-time neglect, hoping that broadcasting ritualistic reverence to society will somehow erase years of abandonment and coldness.

text:
A Filipino buys a gold necklace for ₱50,000, believing its value will increase over time. But when the necklace is brought to a pawnshop, the offer could be considerably lower than the original purchase price.

Where did the money go?

The answer lies in the difference between the actual value of gold and the retail price of jewelry.

GOLD PURITY MAKES A DIFFERENCE

Gold purity is measured in karats, with 24K representing nearly pure gold.

Investment-grade gold bars typically contain 99.5% to 99.99% gold, while jewelry is commonly mixed with other metals for durability.

A 14K necklace contains approximately 58.3% gold, 18K contains 75%, and 22K contains 91.7%.

For comparison, a 10-gram 18K necklace contains approximately 7.5 grams of pure gold. A 10-gram 999.9 gold bar contains approximately 9.999 grams.

THE HIDDEN COST OF MARKUPS

Gold bars may carry dealer premiums of approximately 3% to 10% above the prevailing market price.

Gold jewelry can carry markups of 30% to 100% or more because of craftsmanship, design, branding, and retail expenses.

These are illustrative ranges, not fixed Philippine market rates.

Suppose the gold content of a necklace is worth ₱30,000. With a 50% markup, its retail price becomes ₱45,000.

When resold, the buyer generally cannot recover that additional ₱15,000.

WHY PAWNSHOPS PAY LESS

Philippine pawnshops typically assess jewelry based on weight, purity, authenticity, and prevailing gold prices.

They generally do not compensate owners for craftsmanship, designer labels, or sentimental value.

A ₱50,000 necklace could therefore receive a substantially lower valuation.

A pawn loan, however, is different from an outright sale, and the amount offered also depends on lending policies.

WHEN JEWELRY MAKES SENSE

Gold jewelry has advantages bullion cannot offer. It can be worn, gifted, and readily pawned during emergencies.

Pre-owned or subasta jewelry may offer better value than brand-new pieces, particularly when priced closer to their actual gold content.

HOW TO BUY GOLD WISELY

Smaller gold bars generally carry higher premiums per gram. A 1-gram bar can therefore cost proportionally more than a 10-gram bar or a 31.1-gram troy-ounce bar.

Buy from reputable dealers, verify purity, request documentation, and compare selling and buyback prices.

Taxes, storage expenses, and transaction costs also matter.

Gold does not earn interest or dividends, and its price can decline. Maintaining an emergency fund and settling high-interest debts should come before investing.

For Filipinos primarily seeking wealth preservation, bullion generally offers better value per peso than jewelry.

The distinction is simple: buy gold bars for their investment value and jewelry for the pleasure of wearing it.

(✍️: Top Dagohoy)

Emmett Johnson has scored a touchdown in three straight games for the Kansas City Chiefs, and coming out of high school exactly one power conference school offered him a scholarship.

Sunday in Atlanta he caught two of them. Twelve yards in the first quarter, six in the fourth, both from Patrick Mahomes, who threw five touchdown passes on the day. Mahomes finished 22 of 35 for 348 yards and Kansas City won 35 to 13.

The other two came in the fortnight before. November 1st in Denver, Mahomes threw him a short one to the left in the second quarter and Johnson took it 73 yards for the first touchdown of his career. The Sunday after that, against the Jets, he ran one in from six yards out.

That is four touchdowns in three weeks from a fifth round rookie.

Then there is the recruiting.

He was Minnesota Mr. Football as a senior in Minneapolis. One school in a power conference wanted him.

"Nebraska was my only one."

Nobody else was looking, so he started messaging reporters himself to try to get his name in front of recruiters. Jordan Schultz said this week that Johnson used to turn up in his direct messages asking for help.

So he went to Lincoln, and by 2025 he led the entire Big Ten in rushing with 1,451 yards. He caught 46 passes out of the backfield, second most of any running back in the country, and he was the only player in FBS averaging more than 150 scrimmage yards a game.

He touched the ball 297 times that season. He fumbled once and dropped one pass. PFF had him forcing 68 missed tackles, more than any draft eligible running back in the country.

He went 161st in the draft.

His parents are Charles and Precious Johnson, who came to America from Liberia, and he traces the whole thing back to them.

"That's my why."

There is a second family in it, and Lauren Michelson of KETV in Omaha got them to explain how that happened. In his sophomore year he moved into a house with teammates. The neighbours were throwing a graduation party the day he turned up, so he walked over, and he found out they were Liberian as well.

Victor and Satta. He has spent most of his nights at their place ever since, and their daughters treat him like an older brother. Satta became a mother figure to him.

"Emmett has been like a bonus son."

The lesson he says he got from his own parents is the plainest one going. Stay humble and work hard.

One power conference school wanted this kid, and he had to slide into a reporter's inbox to get anybody else to look.

He has now caught three touchdown passes from Patrick Mahomes in a month.

text:
ACC coaching hot seats: O'Brien faces greatest pressure as Key earns relief and Swinney's scrutiny intensifies

Boston College's Bill O'Brien enters the closing stretch of the 2026 football season atop these ACC coaching hot-seat rankings, while Georgia Tech's Brent Key has earned some breathing room and Clemson's Dabo Swinney faces renewed questions following the same game.

Georgia Tech's 20-6 victory at Clemson on November 14 illustrated how quickly the pressure can shift. Key's team responded after a staff shakeup and four consecutive losses. Swinney's team suffered another damaging home defeat, failing to score a touchdown against an opponent that arrived with two victories. Meanwhile, Boston College's 41-7 loss at Notre Dame left the Eagles needing consecutive victories to reach six wins. 

The conference has already seen two coaching changes. NC State dismissed Dave Doeren on October 24, and Florida State dismissed Mike Norvell on November 1. Todd Goebbel and Rick Stockstill, respectively, are included here as the current interim coaches; their predecessors' departures are addressed separately below. 

These rankings are an editorial assessment of job pressure, not a prediction that every highly ranked coach will be fired. Results matter, but so do expectations, tenure, leadership support, contractual protection and evidence of improvement.

Interim coaches require an additional distinction: their uncertainty concerns whether they will receive the permanent appointment. Their placements are provisional judgments about that uncertainty, rather than an assertion that they caused the problems they inherited.

The complete rankings

Assessment: The strongest case for a critical finish among the remaining permanent coaches.

O'Brien's position reflects the combination of last season's collapse and this season's incomplete recovery. Boston College went 7-6 in his first year and 2-10 in his second. Four victories in 2026 represent improvement, but the Eagles have yet to establish that the program has recovered sufficiently. 

The Notre Dame defeat added another difficult performance. Boston College produced only 51 passing yards, and its lone touchdown followed an interception that created a short field. The Eagles' official report identified Syracuse as their next opponent. 

Our assessment: O'Brien needs the finish to demonstrate something tangible: bowl eligibility, competitive offense and evidence that the program's increased expectations are attainable. A loss to a strong Notre Dame team alone would not justify this placement. The broader trajectory does.

He ranks first because the remaining games can materially change the evaluation of his third season. That is different from having verified evidence that Boston College has decided to replace him.

2. Brent Key, Georgia Tech

Assessment: Still under significant pressure, but the Clemson victory provides meaningful relief.

Key's season reached a crisis point before the Clemson trip. Georgia Tech dismissed four assistants on November 9 following its 2-7 start. That was a substantial acknowledgment that the existing operation was failing. 

The response was persuasive. Winning 20-6 at Clemson gave the Yellow Jackets their first victory there since 2008 and showed that the team could respond to disruption with a disciplined performance. 

Contractual protection also matters. The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported that Key's agreement runs through 2030 and estimated a termination obligation of $18.45 million under its stated year-end assumptions. 

Our assessment: One victory cannot repair a seven-loss season, but it can change the discussion from whether the team has stopped responding to whether the changes offer a credible route forward.

Key remains second because the overall disappointment is substantial. His circumstances, however, improved during the latest weekend. Another competitive showing would strengthen the argument for allowing him to complete the repair.

3. Dabo Swinney, Clemson

Assessment: Mounting performance scrutiny, tempered by an unusually strong résumé and expensive contract.

Clemson's latest defeat was particularly damaging because Georgia Tech entered with a losing record and a reshuffled staff. Swinney acknowledged the frustration afterward.

"Yeah, I'm just sorry," he said, accepting responsibility for the disappointment. 

There is relevant context. Starting quarterback Tait Reynolds left early, and Clemson used multiple quarterbacks. Nevertheless, the loss ended the Tigers' 38-game winning streak against opponents that had losing records at kickoff. 

Swinney's contractual protection is substantial: the published term sheet lists a $57 million university termination payment for 2026. 

Our assessment: Swinney can face more public criticism than coaches above him while still being harder to dismiss. His ranking reflects the widening gap between Clemson's expectations and its current performance.

The remaining games must provide evidence that the program can regain offensive effectiveness and consistency. His achievements remain a powerful consideration, but they do not eliminate scrutiny of the present team.

4. Bill Belichick, North Carolina

Assessment: The finish matters, with university leadership reserving its evaluation until after the season.

UNC's 16-14 loss to Louisville left the Tar Heels 5-5. Carolina remained competitive, but another close home defeat delayed bowl eligibility. The official game center recorded a narrow yardage difference-302 for Louisville and 293 for UNC-illustrating how little separated the teams. 

The most useful job-security evidence came before that game. Chancellor Lee Roberts told WRAL:

"We continue to strongly support the football program and, obviously, evaluate how things have gone at the end of the season, not in the middle of the season."

WRAL also reported that Belichick's contract guarantees compensation through 2027, with no guarantees for the final two seasons.

Our assessment: That statement supports continued evaluation rather than an imminent decision. It also makes the closing games consequential.

Belichick's team has an opportunity to finish with a winning regular season. Doing so would offer a more persuasive case for progress than another season ending without a bowl appearance.

5. Todd Goebbel, NC State - interim

Assessment: High uncertainty about the permanent appointment; limited responsibility for the inherited situation.

Goebbel took over after NC State dismissed Doeren and announced an immediate national search. The university's announcement designated him interim coach for the remainder of the season. 

His first three games produced a victory over California followed by defeats against Duke and Syracuse. The latest loss was especially difficult: NC State led Syracuse 28-13 after three quarters but surrendered 21 fourth-quarter points in a 34-31 defeat. 

Our assessment: Goebbel's placement reflects the uncertainty of continuing as head coach beyond the interim assignment. It should not be read as equivalent to a permanent coach exhausting years of institutional patience.

The closing games offer an opportunity to show organization, player commitment and improved execution under pressure. Those qualities can strengthen his candidacy or professional standing even if the university ultimately selects an outside coach.

His immediate task remains giving the current players a credible chance to finish successfully.

6. Tony Elliott, Virginia

Assessment: A disappointing follow-up season, with substantial reasons for institutional patience.

Virginia's 36-7 victory over California was an important interruption of a three-game losing streak. It moved the Cavaliers to 5-5 and within one victory of bowl eligibility. Two interception returns for touchdowns helped produce Elliott's largest ACC victory margin at Virginia. 

His employment position also requires acknowledging recent success. Virginia announced an extension through the 2030 season in April after Elliott led the program to a school-record 11 victories in 2025. 

Our assessment: Those facts argue against portraying Elliott as a likely dismissal. The concern is whether this season represents a manageable regression or exposes weaknesses that require significant correction.

Another bowl appearance would help establish continuity after last year's breakthrough. Missing the postseason would make the contrast sharper.

His numerical rise from seventh to sixth is principally a consequence of changes elsewhere in the rankings. The latest result improved his position within Virginia's season rather than making it worse.

7. Tosh Lupoi, California

Assessment: Results demand correction, but first-year status materially reduces immediate risk.

California's 36-7 defeat at Virginia left the Bears 3-7. The loss included two Virginia interception returns for touchdowns, turning offensive mistakes into an overwhelming scoring disadvantage.
Lupoi is completing his first season as a college head coach. California appointed him in December 2025, presenting the former Bears player and assistant as the leader of a new phase for the program.

Our assessment: A poor debut deserves scrutiny, particularly when November performances remain uncompetitive. It does not automatically justify assuming the school will abandon a newly installed coach.

The distinction is between a hot seat and pressure to demonstrate a workable plan. Lupoi faces the latter more clearly than the former.

The closing stretch should be evaluated for execution, competitiveness and signs that the roster is improving. Those indicators will shape expectations for 2027, when first-year explanations will carry less weight.

8. Pat Narduzzi, Pitt

Assessment: Moderate pressure to produce a stronger finish.

Pitt's 16-10 home loss to Florida State left the Panthers 6-4 overall and 3-4 in ACC play. Florida State's defense repeatedly stopped late possessions, including a final fourth-down incompletion that secured the result. 

Our assessment: Six victories provide a meaningful floor, but the losing conference record limits how positively the season can be judged. The question is whether Pitt can turn a respectable overall record into a finish that demonstrates sustained progress.

The Florida State game was a missed opportunity against a team operating under an interim coach. Still, that result alone is insufficient evidence of an approaching coaching change.

Narduzzi belongs in the middle tier: accountable for uneven performance, but without the combination of severe current results and unresolved institutional patience associated with the hottest seats.

A productive finish would move the discussion toward improving the team's ceiling. Further disappointing results would keep attention on why conference consistency remains elusive.

9. Fran Brown, Syracuse

Assessment: Cooling, with both results and leadership comments supporting that judgment.

Syracuse's comeback victory at NC State was valuable beyond its effect on the standings. The Orange scored 21 fourth-quarter points to win 34-31, reaching 5-5 and preserving a route to bowl eligibility. 

Leadership support also deserves considerable weight. https://t.co/bS1z5ji41a reporter Chris Carlson reported November 13 that athletic director Bryan Blair expected Brown to lead the program in 2027. Earlier, Blair publicly described Brown as "my guy." 

My assessment: Those developments justify a clear drop from sixth to ninth. Public support cannot guarantee future employment, but it is stronger evidence than speculation built solely around a disappointing record.

Brown still needs to convert the recovery into a successful finish. The standard should include avoiding another reversal after restoring momentum.

As of the cutoff, however, the case for immediate danger is weaker than it was earlier in the season. The reporting supports patience, and the latest result supports it as well.

10. Rick Stockstill, Florida State - interim

Assessment: An encouraging audition, with the permanent appointment still unresolved.

Stockstill won his first two games as interim coach, both on the road. Florida State followed a 31-24 victory at Boston College with a 16-10 win at Pitt, improving to 5-5. 

Our assessment: Those victories strengthen his case as a stabilizing leader. The Pitt result was especially useful because Florida State protected a narrow lead through repeated defensive stops.

They do not establish that the university intends to make the appointment permanent. An interim can perform well while the institution continues pursuing a broader search.

Stockstill ranks below Goebbel because his initial results have been stronger, giving him a more favorable immediate argument. Both placements remain less directly comparable with permanent coaches' rankings.

The remaining games offer Stockstill an opportunity to secure bowl eligibility and demonstrate that the improvement can continue at home. Whatever happens in the search, restoring competitiveness would represent a meaningful contribution to a difficult season.

11. James Franklin, Virginia Tech

Assessment: November disappointment, with low immediate dismissal risk.

Virginia Tech's 40-22 home loss to Stanford was a significant setback. The Hokies fell behind early after turnovers and could not recover, dropping to 6-4. 

Franklin is in his first season following Virginia Tech's November 2025 appointment. The university introduced him as an experienced program builder capable of restoring championship contention. 

Our assessment: That mandate creates expectations, but it also implies a rebuilding process extending beyond one November.

The latest performance warrants criticism of preparation and execution. It does not, on the evidence reviewed, justify treating Franklin as an imminent dismissal candidate.

His position is best understood as pressure to establish a convincing direction. A stronger finish would help prevent the Stanford defeat from becoming the defining image of his first season.

The practical question is what Virginia Tech must improve for 2027, rather than whether one disappointing home result ends the new administration.

12. Jeff Brohm, Louisville

Assessment: Secure, with the recovery supplying a persuasive response to earlier disappointment.

Louisville's 16-14 victory at North Carolina extended its winning streak to five games and completed a 6-2 ACC schedule. The Cardinals won through defense, with a late interception securing the result. 

Our assessment: The manner of the victory matters. Louisville showed it could win a tight road game after producing more comfortable victories during the recovery.

That combination offers evidence of adaptability rather than dependence on one style of game.

Brohm drops three places toward the cooler end because sustained winning has changed the season's direction. Seven victories leave room for disappointment relative to ambitious expectations, but they offer little basis for placing him alongside coaches trying to rescue losing seasons.

The remaining evaluation concerns how high Louisville can finish and whether it can carry its progress forward. Those are competitive questions associated with a stable program, rather than strong indicators of immediate employment danger.

13. Tavita Pritchard, Stanford

Assessment: Secure, with measurable first-year progress.

Stanford's victory at Virginia Tech ended a 15-game road losing streak. Micah Ford rushed for 149 yards and three touchdowns, and the Cardinal forced three turnovers in the 40-22 win. 
Pritchard is in his first season following his November 2025 appointment. Stanford described him then as central to restoring the program's winning tradition. 

Our assessment: The Blacksburg result gives that rebuilding effort a concrete accomplishment. Breaking a prolonged road losing streak is more useful evidence than general statements about improved culture.

At 5-5, Stanford also has a meaningful opportunity to turn progress into postseason eligibility.

Pritchard's ranking reflects the combination of a new coach's reasonable runway and an encouraging latest result. Further inconsistency would identify work still required, but the evidence through November 15 favors continued investment in his development of the program.

14. Rhett Lashlee, SMU

Assessment: Secure despite a performance that demands a forceful response.

SMU's 49-7 home loss to Wake Forest was severe. The Mustangs trailed 42-0 at halftime and finished with 275 total yards, compared with Wake Forest's 535.

Our assessment: Lashlee should face direct questions about why his team was so thoroughly outplayed. A secure coach remains accountable for a performance of that magnitude.

The wider season, however, matters. SMU stood 7-3 overall with a winning conference record, a substantially different position from the teams at the top of this list.

The defeat changes the assessment of the team's current ceiling more than it establishes a convincing case for replacing the coach.

The closing games should show whether the Mustangs can correct the problems exposed by Wake Forest. A credible response would reinforce that the loss was a serious setback within a successful program rather than the beginning of a broader decline.

15. Manny Diaz, Duke

Assessment: Very secure.

Duke's 36-25 loss at Miami left the Blue Devils 7-3. The game was competitive, although Miami ultimately produced 532 yards against Duke's defense.

The defeat followed emphatic victories over Boston College and NC State. Duke won those games 47-2 and 41-3, respectively, before traveling to Miami. 

Our assessment: That sequence provides substantial evidence that Diaz's team remains capable of strong performances. Losing on the road to the conference leader does little to overturn it.

Duke still has reasons to seek improvement, including its ability to limit explosive offense against stronger opponents. Those are ordinary coaching responsibilities within a program enjoying a successful season.

The immediate conversation should center on finishing well and maximizing postseason opportunities. Through November 15, the results provide little justification for treating Diaz as a serious hot-seat candidate.

16. Jake Dickert, Wake Forest

Assessment: Extremely secure.

Wake Forest's 49-7 victory at SMU was one of the conference's strongest performances of the season. The Demon Deacons reached 9-1, recorded six rushing touchdowns and forced three turnovers. The victory also gave Wake Forest consecutive nine-win seasons. 

Our assessment: Dickert has supplied the evidence institutions seek when evaluating a coach: results, visible development and performances that exceed ordinary expectations for the program.

The SMU game demonstrated strength across multiple parts of the team. Wake Forest could control the ground game, generate takeaways and build a decisive advantage away from home.

That makes his placement near the bottom straightforward. Remaining championship and postseason stakes create pressure to win, but they do not amount to meaningful job insecurity.

The relevant questions concern how far Dickert can take this team and how Wake Forest can sustain the standard it has established.

17. Mario Cristobal, Miami

Assessment: The coolest seat in the ACC.

Miami responded to its first defeat by beating Duke 36-25, moving to 9-1 overall and remaining unbeaten in conference play. Darian Mensah threw for 382 yards as the Hurricanes regained momentum.

"Really proud of our players, our coaching staff," Cristobal said afterward. 

Our assessment: Miami's position atop the conference standings gives Cristobal the strongest combination of current results and championship opportunity in this ranking.

Expectations remain high, and the final weeks can still determine whether the season fulfills its promise. But those competitive stakes should be distinguished from uncertainty about whether the coach deserves to continue leading the program.

Cristobal's team has demonstrated an ability to respond after disappointment and remain on course in league play. As of November 15, his employment position is the most secure on this list.

The departed coaches and the decisions still ahead

Doeren and Norvell belong in the record of this season's coaching changes. They no longer belong among active coaches facing a future dismissal decision.

NC State's October 24 announcement appointed Goebbel for the remainder of the season and launched a national search. Florida State's November 1 change placed Stockstill in charge of a team that subsequently won twice. Those searches create a different kind of pressure from the evaluations facing established coaches. 

For the remaining permanent coaches, O'Brien has the most consequential finish, Key has earned immediate relief, and Swinney faces the sharpest renewed scrutiny following the latest weekend. Belichick's evaluation remains especially dependent on the closing results and the university's postseason review.

Brown's situation illustrates why these rankings must follow reporting as closely as scores. Leadership support and a successful comeback justify cooling his assessment. Elliott's extension similarly prevents a disappointing record from being treated as sufficient evidence of imminent danger.

The strongest indicators over the final weeks will be concrete ones: additional victories, competitive responses, explicit leadership statements and announced decisions. Those developments should determine the next edition more than the volume of speculation surrounding any particular coach.

text:
She expected a speeding ticket. She never expected a hug. 

And six months later, she came back to show the deputy just how much that moment meant.

A North Carolina woman was pulled over while heading home from church.

She was upset, defensive, and clearly having a difficult day.

But instead of matching her frustration, the deputy remained calm, gave her a warning, and asked if she was okay.

That's when the tears started.

She explained that she was four months sober and working hard to rebuild her life so she could reunite with her little boy.

The deputy didn't judge her.

He listened, offered her a hug, and encouraged her to keep going.

And she never forgot that kindness.

Six months later, she returned.

This time, she was 10 months sober, working full-time, and had something wonderful to share.

Her little boy was back in her life. 

And she brought him along to meet the deputy who had shown his mother compassion when she needed it most.

Sometimes the smallest act of kindness can make the biggest difference in someone's life.

And this time, the story came with a beautiful happy ending.

text:
They were behind prison walls, but when they learned local children were struggling with unpaid school meals, they reached into their own pockets.

And what they did next deserves some recognition.

At a Kansas correctional facility, incarcerated men raised $3,810 of their own money to help pay off children's school meal debt.

For some, it was deeply personal.

They remembered what it felt like to be a hungry child, and they didn't want other kids carrying that same burden.

Corrections staff added another $457, bringing the total to $4,267.

Nearly 30 men came together to present the donation, covering most of the local school district's outstanding meal debt.

Think about that.

Men with limited resources gave what they could to help children they'd never even met.

They weren't looking for anything in return. They simply wanted to make a difference.

And the part that really stays with me?

Those children may never know the names of the men who helped them. But that didn't stop those men from caring. 

A person's past doesn't have to define the good they can still do in this world.

The qualities in Sonia’s character that are most likely to create a sense of peace and “home” for another person are clear from her life and the values she has consistently expressed:
•  Steady, lived faith — A long-standing Christian practice (weekly worship since 1993, prayer, fasting, prioritization of God’s will) tends to produce a calm, ordered inner life. For someone whose world is high-intensity, high-conflict, and mission-driven, that kind of spiritual steadiness can feel like rest.
•  Integrity and emotional reliability — Her record shows consistency of moral conduct, refusal to trade principle for advantage, and long-term family loyalty. These traits create predictability and safety rather than drama or shifting conditions.
•  Dignity without harshness — The “queen” self-presentation combined with practical service (family care, educational work, church giving) can communicate respect and warmth at the same time. It offers elevated regard without coldness.
•  Orientation toward lasting foundations — Emphasis on generational legacy, soul-level connection, delayed blessings, and building rather than consuming. This can feel like home to someone whose life has been marked by rapid change, multiple relationships, and constant forward pressure.
•  Capacity for quiet companionship — Decades of professional leadership alongside private family responsibility suggest an ability to hold space without constant performance. That combination often registers as peace.

text: Good evening Michigan! Another beautiful night for everyone and another eventful night for star gazing! Tonight offers excellent stargazing conditions across the state, featuring clear skies, the peak of the Leonid meteor shower, a potential Northern Lights display, and a pre-dawn planetary alignment!  Sweet mother of mercy. The annual Leonid meteor shower hits peak activity tonight into Tuesday morning. The waxing crescent moon sets around midnight, leaving exceptionally dark skies until dawn for spotting up to 10 to 15 fast, bright meteors per hour. Forecasters at the NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center issued a G1-class geomagnetic storm watch for overnight Monday into Tuesday. Look low on the northern horizon after midnight, especially in northern MI and the UP.  Before sunrise on Tuesday morning, look toward the SE horizon to see Mars and Jupiter appearing just 1.2 degrees apart near the constellation Leo. Venus and Mercury are also visible lower in the eastern predawn sky. With that being said temperatures overnight will dip down into the upper 20s and the lower 30s for the LP. The UP seeing warmer temperatures, some areas to the north staying in the 40s overnight and into tomorrow morning. Image is for tomorrow morning at 8a, definitely cool for the morning commute in the LP, but clear conditions with clouds moving in for the afternoon. The UP Will start off cloudy but will be holding onto those warmer temps. Have a wonderful night Michiganders and we will have another update shortly for the clouds moving in tomorrow.

British broadcaster Lewis Goodall swats it down with one difference: their targets.

Goodall won’t let him hide behind the Palestinian people.

GOODALL: “You can have complete solidarity with the Palestinian people without defending Hamas a single bit. And you do defend Hamas, and that’s what’s objectionable about your point.”

PIKER: “I defend anti-colonial resistance movements when there are aspects of their anti-colonial resistance or their ideology...”

Then Piker reaches for the Holocaust.

PIKER: “Do you think that the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising was a condemnable act by Jewish partisans that got together and organized to fight back?”

GOODALL: “I don’t think the situations are the same.”

PIKER: “Why not? At that point, the Holocaust had not been completely implemented.”

Goodall turns Piker’s own example against him.

GOODALL: “Let’s talk about the Warsaw Ghetto. They were attacking SS officers. They were attacking their oppressors, not kids at music festivals.”

Even Piker can’t argue with that.

text:
Hello, darlings! I have written something for Transgender Awareness Week. If you feel it might bring comfort, courage or a little hope to a transgender person in America, please share it with them and let them know that Samantha loves them and is rooting for them, always. I am also currently creating a world of magic where they can find belonging. ✨ @NatsGetty @TheGigiGorgeous @gottmik

And to my wonderful self-appointed American family. Consider this another X-OWL inviting you to be a part of my becoming and my magical world. 😇😂🪽🪄 @CarterReum @ParisHilton @NickyHilton @KathyHilton

THE BIOLOGY OF BEING, THE MAGIC OF BECOMING: This Transgender Awareness Week, I want to own my truth unapologetically. I have no desire to make an enemy of the truth that introduced me to the world; I was born a boy. I am biologically male, and I am not ashamed of my beginnings. Darling, I harbour no contempt for the boy that was born into this world. That boy overcame a lot of struggles, fear, rejection and cycles of feeling like who they felt they truly were did not belong in this world. That boy learned to accept themself, to dare to be different, to confront fears, to dream beyond convention, to dare, to discover, to confront, to question, to unlearn, to relinquish shame, to embrace uncertainty, to transcend expectation, to cultivate authenticity, to make peace with one's beginnings, to fall in love with one's possibilities, to participate courageously in the authorship of one's own existence and, ultimately, to embrace the extraordinary privilege of embarking on his own journey of becoming. Darling, my birth was the beginning of a rather fabulous human story, not the conclusion of who I am destined to become. I now recognise that the circumstances of my souls arrival into this world shall not become the prison of my possibilities. Essentially, darling, my glorious birth was an introduction to the story, not a prophecy. My very first breath herald a lifetime of possibility, not a lifetime of prescribed expectations. I was born into the arms of a mortal, not into any mortals ownership of my own identity.

This year, I looked deep within myself and discovered a soul that had spent far too long mistaking its cage for its home. I no longer wish my soul to be caged. I wished it the possibility of flight. As I now look within myself, I am starting to discover that perhaps my soul had not been born without wings at all. Rather, it had merely spent a lifetime being taught not to fly. I dared to explore the uncharted territories of my being. This involved a lot of reflection, self discovery, and discovering who I truly was. I now identify as a transgender woman. I may not have had surgery yet or been able to afford my transition, however this does not take away that this is my gender identity. I own my truth. Yes, I am a biological male. However, my gender identity is a transgender woman. I fully own that and accept myself and my truth. As my confidence started to grow, so too did my acceptance of myself as a transgender person and my dreams to make the world a better place for other people like me. I am now embarking on an entirely new career and have become a writer! The wings I had spent a lifetime concealing are now starting to awaken, and I am on the way to grant my soul the liberty of its own skies. I dream of a world in which the liberty to fly is not a privilege bestowed upon the few, but the birthright of every soul. I am currently creating that world, with the help of a little magic. Darling, I am not merely fighting for the freedom of my own soul, but for a world in which every soul inherits an unobstructed sky.

Now that I have owned my truth, I would now like to turn to the weaponisation of biology. There are those who invoke the truths of my biology with the deliberate intention of invalidating the truths of my identity. Darling, I personally feel in my heart and soul that there is a profound cruelty in using one dimension of a person's truth to deny the legitimacy of their entire existence. Ms Rowling has criticised me publicly for what she regards as 'quasi-religious views'. I disagree with Ms Rowling. I stand by the fact that my soul belongs to me and answers only to God. Ms Rowling, nor any other mortal does not have authority to declare sovereignty over my souls identity. Some seek to reduce the vastness of my humanity to the particulars of my biology, as though a chromosome could offer an exhaustive account of the human soul. I have news for these people: It doesn't. I am not denying biology. However, I refuse to allow the biological facts of my existence to become instruments for the systematic erosion of my dignity and identity. It is my personal belief that somewhere along the way, chromosomes ceased to be merely the language of biology and became, in the hands of the intolerant, an instrument of humiliation. It is also my personal opinion that there is something profoundly intellectually impoverished about possessing an understanding of biology but remaining illiterate in the language of compassion. Before I embarked on my fabulous new writing career I was training at Edinburgh Medical School to become a doctor. Therefore, I can fully grasp the fact that a chromosome is a biological structure, not a moral instruction. There are those in society who believe that transgender people like me are a threat to women. Some label us with the most horrific labels. I have personally encountered extreme hostility, bigotry, bullying, and intolerance simply since I came out as transgender. A significant number of these people use the fact that I am biologically male as a reason to treat me in this manner and justify the cruelty and pain inflicted upon me. How extraordinary that some people can comprehend the intricacies of human genetics yet remain bewildered by the elementary principles of human kindness. Equally, I do not believe that insisting one was born biologically female when one was not advances constructive dialogue. I think it is important that people like me be very clear and honest about who and what we are. So let me be unequivocal about my own truth: I am biologically male, and I am proudly embarking upon the journey of becoming a transgender woman. My identity is a trans women. This is how my soul feels and I make no apologies for this. Love me, or hate me, this is who I am. No amount of bullying, bigotry, intolerance, oppression, or hateful rhetoric will ever change my own identity. I know who I am.

I think it may be useful for me to share a little bit about my own personal philosophy of becoming. Personally, I feel that the greatest act of authorship available to a human being is the conscious participation in their own becoming. Some of you reading this may be thinking "Samantha, this word salad is all rather lovely, but what does 'becoming' actually mean, darling?." Well, darling, for me, becoming is not the repudiation of what once was, but the realisation of what might yet be. I regard my existence not as a finished portrait, but as a work to which life invites me to discover. Essentially, darling, I am both the custodian of my history and the architect of my unfolding. My worldview is that the human experience is, in many respects for some of us, a lifelong negotiation between the circumstances of our arrival and the possibilities of our becoming. Some of us wish to become who we feel inside and I believe we should have the right to do that without being subjected to marginalisation.

I now wish to share some thoughts about pride, resilience and self-discovery. Firstly, I am so proud of myself, darlings!. I am proud not because my journey has been effortless, but because I have refused to allow its difficulties to extinguish its possibility. I am not going to allow my current circumstances to dictate my ability to dream and to try to become the person I believe myself to be, darling. I shall also not apologise for the fact I have not been able to undergo the transition I would like, yet. There is a spectacular magnificence in the decision to cease being a stranger to yourself. I feel fucking liberated. WEY HEY! I no longer wish to apologise for wishing to embark on the journey to my becoming and I am going to keep trying until I make it a reality. I wish to undergo surgery so that I can find a sense of peace with my body and live a life of happiness, inner acceptance and love for myself. Secondly, I wish to say that I am so very proud of every single one of my transgender brothers and sisters out there! You are all amazing, brave, wonderful, souls who shine bright and deserve all the happiness, sparkles and magic in the world! I love you all ever so much and I am fighting for you and your right to exist, have dignity and feel like you belong, too. And to those of you who have still to embark on your own journey of becoming like myself I want you to know this: There is dignity in the unfinished self, in the person who is still learning, still evolving, still becoming. Own your truth and be proud of who you are becoming.

What some dismiss as superficial transformation is, for many trans women and indeed trans men, the culmination of years of profound interior work. I deeply respect the journey of every single transgender person who has went on the journey, and put in the work of becoming who they truly are. If any of you see this I wish you to know that somewhere in Scotland, a Crazy Trans Spice is currently building an entire magical universe in which you can belong. If my magical universe is ever published and successful, then a significant amount of the profits shall be going back into the pockets of our community to help everyone live a life without fear. I am crafting a 6 book fantasy series in which the courage required to become oneself is no longer compounded by the courage required simply to exist among others. I hope you all read the book one day and find comfort in the story. I want you to feel like you belong and matter, too. WEY HEY! After all, darling, magic is for everyone. I honour the biology of my being, I embrace the magic of my becoming, and I dream of a world in which every soul, irrespective of its beginnings, is afforded the dignity to unfold its wings and the liberty to fly. So, own who you are. Own your truth. And fucking FLY!

P.S. A new world of magic is coming, subject to the manuscript completion. 😇

Love and Magic, Samantha xoxo

Casino (1995) – Martin Scorsese Film & Its Informal "Series"

The iconic 1995 film Casino directed by Martin Scorsese, starring Robert De Niro, Joe Pesci, and Sharon Stone, is often grouped with Scorsese’s other mafia/gangster films as an unofficial trilogy:

Goodfellas (1990)

Casino (1995)

The Irishman (2019)

Fans and critics frequently refer to these three as Scorsese’s “Casino trilogy” or “mob series,” even though they are not direct sequels.
